topic: Revive parent stat_dp_cate_uniform_design_nuisance_privacy_frontier by proving a log-free target-fiber private T-estimation theorem on the unchanged exact-uniform Hölder pointwise-CATE class. Construct one finite pure-DP estimator from Bernoulli reduction, coherent composite threshold tests, finite wavelet profiles, and scalar-shell exponential selection, and establish R_DP equivalent to max{R_NP,r_G,r_F} without assuming a formula for R_NP, using the separate nonprivate converse, stabilizing an unspecified minimax estimator, or retaining a nuisance-net logarithm. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Independent Bernoullization of bounded outcomes exactly preserves the propensity, arm means, CATE, and both full-class nonprivate and pure-DP minimax risks. Nonprivate minimax risk controls each composite threshold error, while an integrated absolute-risk identity gives a coherent nested family; summing the two candidates per scalar distance shell removes output-cardinality logarithms for stable scores. A finite d=1 randomized-treatment estimator attains max(n^-1/3,(n epsilon)^-1/2) without logs. On the parent’s coupled-nuisance component, singleton mixtures coincide but exact two-record TV equals 4ab and a bounded pair statistic has mean ±4ab, yielding log-free private pair testing. No counterexample forcing a log or third privacy radius was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: At the same sample size, construct full-class stable composite scores whose distance-weighted shell errors sum independently of nuisance-sieve size, proving nuisance-entropy cancellation and that Hamming stabilization adds only r_G and r_F for arbitrary least-favorable priors. EARLY KILL TEST: On a finite d=1 two-resolution wavelet family with alpha=beta=1/8 and gamma=1 containing both constant-mixture and shared-sign witnesses, compute nonprivate and private finite programs at the same n, verify every neighboring quantized dataset, and grow the nuisance-sign dimension; a persistent entropy penalty or reliance on the excluded nonprivate formula kills the route. open_problems.why_unsolved: The nonprivate theory supplies the destination class and minimax benchmark, while existing private CATE work does not characterize its pure-DP frontier. The closest general T-mechanism pays for selection over a finite cover. Meanwhile, the parent establishes the privacy lower envelope and only a conditional upper envelope based on an explicit attainable benchmark: scalar minimax risk alone provides no neighboring-record sensitivity certificate. A successful proof must convert risk control into coherent tests between composite CATE fibers, stabilize those tests, and aggregate them by scalar distance without counting nuisance profiles.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fully specified finite pure-DP estimator and uniform absolute-risk theorem proving R_DP(n,epsilon) is equivalent to max{R_NP(n),r_G(n,epsilon),r_F(n,epsilon)}, together with the separate same-class converse and constants independent of nuisance-sieve size.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from heterogeneous-effect motivation to a precisely parameterized Hölder model, a phase-transition frontier, and an explicit attaining construction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CATE is the individualized causal target -> coupled nuisance smoothness determines the nonprivate pointwise frontier -> privacy adds two distinguishability radii -> a target-fiber mechanism must combine all three scales without entropy loss

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the clipped log-likelihood scores, bounded-Hamming-sensitivity proof, and T-mechanism, replacing the global finite-cover union bound by scalar-shell aggregation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest general pure-DP test-to-estimator construction and exposes the precise logarithmic step that must be removed.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over randomized clamped-likelihood testing and its sharp privacy-versus-testing-advantage proof to pairwise target-fiber tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed estimator is assembled from stable tests, and this supplies the sharp binary private-testing template without an output-catalogue penalty.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse the localized higher-order projection and bias-variance decomposition to calibrate finite wavelet profiles and the nonprivate component of the risk.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It attains the exact destination class's nonprivate pointwise risk and identifies the nuisance-interaction geometry the private scores must preserve.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic private hypothesis selection and the published T-mechanism charge a logarithm for the number of candidates. Scalar noise mechanisms avoid this only after a single globally sensitive statistic is available. The parent donor construction controls one specially engineered pair of nuisance mixtures, whereas the desired estimator needs simultaneous nested tests for many composite fibers. Separately optimal tests need not be coherent across thresholds, and a union bound over nuisance profiles restores the forbidden logarithm. The missing argument must show that only a bounded error mass contributes per scalar-distance shell, irrespective of the shell's nuisance multiplicity.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A conversion theorem giving explicit coherence, stability, and shell-summability conditions under which composite tests produce an epsilon-DP scalar estimator with expected loss bounded by the nonprivate testing radius joined with r_G and r_F, with no cover-size factor.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its general-estimation framing, local-modulus benchmark, and isolation of the logarithmic loss as the point of departure.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Private estimation should adapt to local statistical difficulty -> stable tests yield a universal T-mechanism -> generic selection pays model-cover entropy -> ordered causal target fibers may permit shell counting instead

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the construction of a T-estimator from simultaneous tests between metric balls, exploiting nested one-dimensional target balls rather than treating all model points symmetrically.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired theorem modifies the aggregation geometry of the same composite-test architecture.

method_exemplars.technique: Retain shifted clipped-likelihood scores and their Hamming-sensitivity proof, but reorganize exponential selection by scalar shells and integrate its loss tail directly.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This targets the sole cover-cardinality step separating the published guarantee from the desired log-free conversion.

method_exemplars.technique: Use geometrically decaying shell mass, analogous to the staircase mechanism's scalar noise law, to control the selector's partition function.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates how scalar geometry can replace flat output counting, although new analysis is required for data-dependent composite scores.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether independent recordwise Bernoullization gives exact finite-sample equality of the bounded-outcome and binary-outcome full-class pointwise-CATE minimax risks for both unrestricted estimators and pure-DP estimators.

source_refs.claim: The Hölder pointwise-CATE model permits bounded outcomes, while its target and nuisance restrictions are expressed through propensity and conditional arm means.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

open_problems.why_unsolved: Bernoullization preserves conditional means and is recordwise randomized preprocessing, while binary laws form a subclass of the bounded-outcome experiment. Exact two-sided minimax equality nevertheless requires both inequalities at the level of decision problems: the preprocessing direction must preserve every Hölder and overlap restriction and map replacement neighbors to mixtures of replacement neighbors, while the subclass direction must remain valid after restricting the infimum to pure-DP mechanisms. The mined literature and parent artifacts use Bernoulli subclasses for lower bounds but do not state this full experiment-equivalence result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit pair of experiment comparisons proving exact equality of bounded- and Bernoulli-outcome minimax absolute risks, separately for unrestricted and epsilon-DP decision rules, with direct verification of propensity, arm means, CATE, Hölder membership, and replacement adjacency.

writing_exemplar.why: Its model specification makes explicit which experiment restrictions depend only on propensity and conditional arm means.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sharp CATE minimax theory permits bounded outcomes -> binary outcomes provide a tractable least-favorable subclass -> Bernoulli preprocessing preserves the causal means -> exact decision-theoretic equivalence would reduce both private and nonprivate proofs to a finite alphabet

method_exemplars.technique: Use coupling-based central-DP experiment comparison for the Bernoulli-subclass inequality and a recordwise Markov kernel for the reverse inequality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resolution is a two-sided comparison of statistical experiments under a privacy-constrained decision class.

method_exemplars.technique: Track the exact Hölder restrictions, overlap condition, and localized absolute-risk target through the outcome-randomization kernel.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It defines the destination experiment and minimax risk whose preservation must be proved.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Simple-hypothesis private Neyman-Pearson theory relies on additive one-record likelihood increments, but those increments are powerless when the two nuisance mixtures have identical singleton laws. The first informative contrast is then a two-record kernel. A usable upper bound must establish its expectation uniformly over both composite fibers, control replacement sensitivity despite overlapping pairs, and avoid union-bounding over a growing nuisance-sign prior. Existing mixture-coupling results furnish converses, and the sparse-component donor handles one fixed prior pair, but neither gives the required dimension-free composite pair-test upper theorem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit bounded pair or decoupled U-statistic test, a pure-DP implementation with an all-neighbor sensitivity proof, and matching uniform upper and lower separation radii for the coupled-nuisance CATE fibers with constants independent of nuisance-sign dimension.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its explanation of why nuisance interaction creates a distinct low-smoothness difficulty and its use of localized fuzzy hypotheses.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Pointwise CATE combines regression and functional-estimation difficulty -> nuisance perturbations can cancel in singleton mixtures -> information first appears through higher-order interactions -> a private pair test must recover it without paying nuisance entropy

method_exemplars.technique: Replace the one-record clamped log-likelihood increment by a bounded two-record contrast and adapt the soft-threshold privacy and testing-advantage proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the sharp binary private-test template; the first proof step that changes is additivity over individual records.

method_exemplars.technique: Use mixture couplings and expected Hamming transport to prove the matching private converse for pair-sensitive least-favorable priors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its lower-bound machinery accommodates mixture hypotheses and relates their indistinguishability directly to central-DP testing risk.

method_exemplars.technique: Insert the pair tests into a target-indexed T-estimator and analyze scalar-distance shells instead of enumerating nuisance profiles.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A successful pair test becomes a full estimator through precisely this stable test-to-estimation conversion.

literature_map:
Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2203.00837) give the closest nonprivate anchor: sharp pointwise Hölder-CATE minimax rates, fuzzy-hypothesis lower bounds, and a localized higher-order R-learner.
Kennedy (2023, Electronic Journal of Statistics, arXiv:2004.14497) develops doubly robust local-polynomial CATE estimation and isolates products of nuisance errors, but has no privacy constraint.
Niu et al. (2022, CLeaR, arXiv:2202.11043) provide a compositional DP meta-algorithm for heterogeneous effects rather than a minimax theorem.
Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025, ICLR, arXiv:2503.03486) add Neyman orthogonality and an RKHS CATE release but do not characterize the pure-DP Hölder pointwise frontier.
Asi, Duchi, Haque, Li, and Ruan (2024, COLT) are the central method anchor: stable clipped-likelihood tests yield universal scalar private estimation only up to logarithmic factors.
Asi, Duchi, and Talwar (2025, arXiv:2503.17252) obtain stability-certified single-parameter releases in parametric M-estimation; their conditions do not settle nonparametric pure-DP target fibers.
Canonne, Kamath, McMillan, Smith, and Ullman (2019, STOC, arXiv:1811.11148) sharply solve pure-DP simple testing with clamped likelihood ratios, but not composite mixtures whose singleton laws coincide.
Acharya, Sun, and Zhang (2021, ALT, arXiv:2004.06830) supply central-DP Le Cam, Fano, and Assouad lower bounds through mixture couplings and expected Hamming transport.
Bun, Kamath, Steinke, and Wu (2021, IEEE TIT, arXiv:1905.13229) show that generic private hypothesis selection pays log m, identifying the entropy cost a shell argument must avoid.
Birgé (2006, Annales IHP, doi:10.1016/j.anihpb.2005.04.004) supplies the nonprivate composite-test and T-estimator architecture behind the modern mechanism.
Asi, Ullman, and Zakynthinou (2023, ICML, arXiv:2302.01855) connect robust and pure-private estimation, but their black-box route does not establish nuisance-entropy cancellation for this CATE class.
Lalanne, Garivier, and Gribonval (2023, TMLR, arXiv:2306.14535), together with Wasserman and Zhou (2010, JASA, arXiv:0811.2501), show how central privacy changes nonparametric rates and motivate projection constructions, but address density rather than causal nuisance fibers.
McSherry and Talwar (2007, FOCS) and Geng and Viswanath (2016, IEEE TIT, arXiv:1212.1186) supply exponential-selection and geometric scalar-shell precedents; no located paper combines them with coherent composite CATE threshold tests to remove nuisance-cover logarithms.
prior_proposal_map:
The highest-priority source was banked parent stat_dp_cate_uniform_design_nuisance_privacy_frontier/v1: its proto_core OEQ, writeup scope, README, five angle reviews, and terminal general and rubric reviews were mined.
Its sole explicit unresolved kernel is symbolic-private-transfer below the nuisance elbow; reviewers repeatedly identify the absence of a risk-only neighboring-dataset stability interface.
The parent also explicitly leaves epsilon_n<n^-1, bounded-density upper transfer, and deterministic uniform-grid designs outside its theorem.
The grandparent stat_dp_cate_minimax_v1/holder_central_dp was inspected; its broad frontier question was largely advanced by the parent, while its reviewers confirm that observational nuisance-private geometry remains live.
Adjacent stat_cate_uniform_sparse_component_converse/v1 was mined as a technique donor: exact singleton cancellation, component factorization, and spanning-tree summation are proved for one fixed pair of Bernoulli prior mixtures.
That donor does not supply uniform composite target-fiber tests, nuisance-entropy cancellation, pure-DP stabilization, or bounded-outcome/Bernoulli experiment equivalence.
The rejected angle in stat_dp_cate_common_support_hypercube_frontier/v1 was inspected; its paired-microcell branch failed Hölder smoothness, while its switched-angle reviews preserve the broader private-design gap.
No legacy proposal TeX or angle-rejected artifact existed for the named parent; the relevant rejected artifact was the common-support sibling's proto_core_angle0_rejected.json.
